concerns.text: T037 (Data Unavailable halt if n < 5) precedes T019 (LOOCV logic for n < 50). This creates a semantic ordering violation: the consumer (LOOCV logic in T019) is blocked by a producer (T037) that destroys the data required for the consumer to function. The Plan explicitly defines a fallback to LOOCV for 5 <= n < 50, but T037 halts the pipeline before T019 can execute this logic.

T020c (Calculate R² drop) is listed before T021b (Stress-Label Permutation Control Test) in the task list, but T020c's logic explicitly depends on reading `results/shuffle_control.json` produced by T021b. A consumer (T020c) cannot run before its producer (T021b) generates the required artifact.

T021a (Null Model comparison) is listed after T020c, but SC-001 requires comparing against a Null Model (predicting mean). T021a is the only task implementing this, yet T020c (which calculates a 'drop' metric) appears to rely on baseline comparisons that should logically follow the Null Model definition. More critically, T020c calculates a drop against the Shuffled Baseline (T021b), not the Null Model (T021a), creating a dependency gap where the metric logic (T020c) does not align with the required baseline (T021a) defined in SC-001.

T018 (Calculate Data Completeness) is marked unimplemented and listed as a prerequisite checkpoint for US1, yet it depends on the output of T014 (pipeline.py). While T014 is implemented, T018 is not. This creates a blocking dependency where the 'fully functional' checkpoint for US1 cannot be verified because the verification task (T018) is missing.

T020a (Raw Feature Baseline) and T021b (Stress-Shuffled Baseline) are listed as separate tasks, but the Plan's SC-002 logic requires calculating the 'drop' against the Raw Feature Baseline (T020). The current task list has T020c calculating the drop against the Shuffled Baseline (T021b). This is a semantic ordering/logic mismatch: the task calculating the metric (T020c) is consuming the wrong producer (T021b) instead of the required producer (T020a) defined in the Plan.
